enzyme_name: Chloromuconate cycloisomerase (dehalogenating cycloisomerase of the modified ortho / chlorocatechol pathway)
organism_context: Pseudomonas sp. P51 and related chloroaromatic degraders (MetaCyc PWY-6094, 3,4,6-trichlorocatechol degradation); enolase-superfamily Mn2+ enzyme.
rationale: Chloromuconate cycloisomerases catalyse cycloisomerisation and the accompanying chloride elimination in one active site as a mechanistically coupled lactonisation/anti-elimination, i.e. one catalytic activity (EC 5.5.1.7) rather than two fused ones; the enzyme acting on 2,3,5-trichloromuconate is assigned from pathway context rather than a dedicated paper on this substrate.
direction_note: The step releases free chloride and destroys the conjugated diacid, so it is effectively irreversible in the degradative (written-forward) direction that the LLM council chose; ModelSEED's '<' rests on an unpaired bronze-grade dGPredictor value with no measured support.

enzyme_name: Chlorobenzene reductive dehalogenase (RdhA/CbrA-type corrinoid [4Fe-4S] reductive dehalogenase); 1,2,4-trichlorobenzene -> 1,4-dichlorobenzene
organism_context: Organohalide-respiring anaerobes: Dehalococcoides mccartyi CBDB1 (PceA-orthologous RdhA shown to be induced by and active on 1,2,4-TCB) and Dehalobacter spp.
rationale: The catalytic RdhA subunit carries a single reductive-dehalogenation activity; it functions as a respiratory complex with the separate membrane-anchor polypeptide RdhB, which is a multi-subunit association and not a fused bifunctional enzyme. KEGG R06849 itself carries no EC/KO and is flagged 'unclear reaction', so the enzyme is assigned from the chemistry.
direction_note: Reductive dechlorination is a respiratory half-reaction driven by an external electron donor and chloride release, so it only ever runs in the dechlorinating (written-forward, TCB->DCB) direction; the ModelSEED equation omits both the electron donor and the chloride product, so the ΔG′° behind the '<' call does not describe the real reaction.

enzyme_name: cis-Chlorobenzene (benzene) dihydrodiol dehydrogenase, TcbB
organism_context: Pseudomonas sp. strain P51 (Tn5280), Burkholderia sp. PS12, Pandoraea sp. MCB032; NAD+-dependent short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase.
rationale: TcbB is a standalone NAD+-dependent SDR whose only activity is oxidation of cis-dihydrodiols to the corresponding catechols (shown on a broad panel of cis-dihydrodiols); the multi-protein character of this pathway sits in the upstream chlorobenzene dioxygenase (a four-protein complex), not in this dehydrogenase.
direction_note: NAD+-dependent aromatisation of the dihydrodiol to 3-chlorocatechol is strongly exergonic and is the committed catabolic step, so the written-forward direction (LLM '>') is the physiological one; the eQuilibrator value carries a sentinel-scale uncertainty (~2.4e4) and the dGPredictor value is bronze-grade, so neither supports ModelSEED's '<'.

enzyme_name: Phosphobase N-methyltransferase (PEAMT/PMEAMT, phosphoethanolamine N-methyltransferase family); this step (P-monomethylethanolamine -> P-dimethylethanolamine) is run by the C-terminal MT2 domain
organism_context: Plants (Arabidopsis NMT1/NMT3, spinach, wheat) and nematodes (Haemonchus contortus HcPMT1/HcPMT2, C. elegans) carry two tandem methyltransferase domains on a single ~475-aa chain; Plasmodium falciparum PfPMT is a single-domain enzyme doing all three methylations.
rationale: One polypeptide carries two structurally distinct SAM-dependent methyltransferase active sites with different phosphobase specificities — MT1 methylates phosphoethanolamine, MT2 methylates the mono- and di-methyl phosphobases — and Arabidopsis PMEAMT (a di-domain protein) cannot use phosphoethanolamine at all, so the two domains are genuinely separate catalytic activities rather than one repeated.
direction_note: This reaction is the MT2 domain's job and MT2 also performs the third methylation, so flux is pulled from P-MEA straight through to phosphocholine; SAM-dependent N-methylation is effectively irreversible in vivo, which supports the forward (methylating) direction over ModelSEED's '<'.

enzyme_name: Cytochrome P450 monooxygenase of the bisphenol A degradation system (BisdB) with its ferredoxin partner BisdA
organism_context: Sphingomonas sp. AO1, Sphingobium sp. YC-JY1, Pseudomonas putida YC-AE1 (CYP inhibitor-sensitive BPA degradation).
rationale: The catalytic P450 component is a single-activity monooxygenase and its electron-transfer partner is a separate ferredoxin polypeptide (a multi-component system, not a fused bifunctional enzyme); the assignment is weak because KEGG R06880 lists no EC and no KO, describes the step as 'oxidative cleavage and dimerization' via a possible isopropenylphenol radical, and the dimerisation half may be non-enzymatic.
direction_note: The real chemistry is an O2-consuming P450 oxidation of two BPA molecules, irreversible in the degradative (written-forward) direction, whereas ModelSEED writes a cofactor-free 1:1 interconversion — so the silver-grade ΔG′° behind the '<' call is computed on the wrong reaction.

enzyme_name: 2-Naphthoyl-CoA reductase (NCR), the prototype dearomatizing aryl-CoA reductase
organism_context: Sulfate-reducing enrichment culture N47 (Deltaproteobacteria) and related anaerobic naphthalene degraders; old-yellow-enzyme-family flavoprotein.
rationale: NCR carries a single dearomatizing ene-reductase activity, which it applies twice in succession (2-naphthoyl-CoA -> 5,6-dihydro- -> 5,6,7,8-tetrahydro-2-naphthoyl-CoA) — one activity used repeatedly, not two fused activities. KEGG R06898 writes the step on free acids, but the physiological substrate and product are the CoA thioesters.
direction_note: Ring reduction is the committed, essentially irreversible dearomatization of anaerobic naphthalene catabolism and only ever runs 2-naphthoyl-CoA -> tetrahydro-2-naphthoyl-CoA (the written-forward direction); the ModelSEED equation supplies only 4 H+ with no electron donor and no CoA, so the eQuilibrator ΔG′° driving '<' is physically meaningless.

enzyme_name: 5,6,7,8-Tetrahydro-2-naphthoyl-CoA reductase (THNCoA reductase), an ATP-independent class/type III aryl-CoA reductase
organism_context: Sulfate-reducing culture N47; homologous to the AprB/AprC type III aryl-CoA reductases of anaerobic phenanthrene degradation.
rationale: The characterised enzyme is a single-activity ring reductase, but KEGG R06899 lumps tetrahydro- to decahydro-2-naphthoate, which in the real pathway is at least two further CoA-thioester reduction steps (via hexahydro-2-naphthoyl-CoA), so the 'catalysing enzyme' for the reaction as written is a sequence rather than one protein.
direction_note: All the steps lumped here are reductive and electron-donor-driven in the catabolic (written-forward) direction; the ModelSEED equation carries only 6 H+ as the reductant, so the silver-grade eQuilibrator ΔG′° behind '<' describes a proton-only pseudo-reaction.

enzyme_name: Putative anaerobic tetralin carboxylase (unidentified)
organism_context: Sulfate-reducing enrichment culture from a contaminated aquifer (Annweiler et al.); same culture that activates naphthalene by carboxylation to 2-naphthoate.
rationale: Degradation studies showed tetralin is activated by addition of a C1 unit to give 5,6,7,8-tetrahydro-2-naphthoic acid, exactly paralleling naphthalene -> 2-naphthoate, but no carboxylase protein has been purified, sequenced or assigned a KO/EC for this step, so its functionality cannot be judged.
direction_note: Physiologically this runs as a carboxylation of tetralin, i.e. left-to-right as ModelSEED writes it (the LLM's '>'); ring carboxylation is thermodynamically uphill and is pulled forward by downstream CoA ligation and ring reduction, so the small positive eQuilibrator ΔG′° used for the '<' call cannot settle the direction.

enzyme_name: 2-Naphthoate monooxygenase (Nmo)
organism_context: Burkholderia sp. JT1500, which grows on 2-naphthoate and accumulates 1-hydroxy-2-naphthoate; KEGG KO K14586.
rationale: The oxygenase carries a single hydroxylation activity; KEGG's gene symbol nmoAB indicates a two-component flavin-dependent monooxygenase (oxygenase plus flavin reductase on separate chains), which is a multi-protein system rather than a fused bifunctional enzyme.
direction_note: KEGG's own R06902 includes FADH2 + O2 as co-substrates; ModelSEED strips both, leaving an unbalanced '2-naphthoate <=> 1-hydroxy-2-naphthoate' whose ΔG′° is meaningless, while the real O2-dependent hydroxylation is irreversible in the written-forward direction the LLM chose.

enzyme_name: 2-Hydroxy-8-methylchromene-2-carboxylate isomerase (methyl analogue of 2-hydroxychromene-2-carboxylate isomerase, NahD)
organism_context: Pseudomonas putida G7 (NAH7 plasmid) and homologues in Sphingomonas yanoikuyae B1 and Pseudomonas sp. TA-2; methylnaphthalene degraders for this substituted substrate.
rationale: NahD-type HCCA isomerase is a homodimeric kappa-class-GST-fold protein with a single catalytic activity — the GSH-assisted cis/trans isomerisation (ring opening) of the chromene carboxylate to the benzylidenepyruvate; the bound GSH is a tightly held cofactor and the GST fold is structural homology, not a second transferase activity.
direction_note: Thompson et al. measured Keq = 1.5 for HCCA -> trans-o-hydroxybenzylidenepyruvate, i.e. ΔG′° ≈ −1 kJ/mol in the written-forward direction, which directly contradicts the +15 kJ/mol eQuilibrator/group-contribution estimates ModelSEED's '<' is built on.

enzyme_name: 2-Carboxy-2-hydroxy-8-carboxychromene isomerase (carboxy analogue of 2-hydroxychromene-2-carboxylate isomerase, NahD)
organism_context: NahD-type isomerases of naphthalene/naphthoate-degrading Pseudomonas and Sphingomonas; the carboxy-substituted substrate arises in naphthalene-dicarboxylate/2-naphthoate branches.
rationale: Assigned by analogy to NahD, a kappa-class-GST-fold homodimer whose only catalytic activity is the GSH-assisted chromene-carboxylate to benzylidenepyruvate isomerisation; no paper characterises an enzyme acting specifically on the 8-carboxy substrate, hence low confidence on enzyme identity (the mono/poly call follows the family).
direction_note: The parent reaction has a measured Keq of 1.5 in the written-forward direction (ΔG′° ≈ −1 kJ/mol), so the identical +15 kJ/mol eQuilibrator estimate that ModelSEED applies to all three chromene isomerases in this chunk is very likely wrong in sign.

enzyme_name: 2-Hydroxy-7-hydroxymethylchromene-2-carboxylate isomerase (hydroxymethyl analogue of 2-hydroxychromene-2-carboxylate isomerase, NahD)
organism_context: NahD-type isomerases of methylnaphthalene-degrading Pseudomonas/Sphingomonas, acting on the hydroxymethyl-substituted ring-fission product.
rationale: Same enzyme family as rxn04721/rxn04731 — a kappa-class-GST-fold homodimer with a single GSH-dependent isomerase activity — but no characterisation exists for the hydroxymethyl substrate specifically, so enzyme identity is inferred from the chemistry.
direction_note: The catabolic pathway only ever runs chromene-carboxylate -> benzylidenepyruvate (written-forward), and the measured Keq = 1.5 for the parent reaction contradicts the positive ΔG′° used for ModelSEED's '<'.

enzyme_name: Adipyl-CoA (dicarboxylyl-CoA) dehydrogenase, DcaA
organism_context: Acinetobacter sp./baylyi ADP1 dca operon for beta-oxidation of straight-chain dicarboxylates; equivalent activity in Pseudomonas putida adipate catabolism. KEGG KO K06446.
rationale: DcaA is an acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (ACAD) family flavoprotein carrying one catalytic activity; the genuinely bifunctional protein of this pathway is the downstream enoyl-CoA hydratase/3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase (FadB/DcaH type), not the dehydrogenase that runs this reaction.
direction_note: ACADs pass electrons to ETF rather than to free FAD, so the FAD/FADH2 formulation ModelSEED uses makes the ΔG′° behind the '<' call unphysiological; the catabolic enzyme runs adipyl-CoA -> 5-carboxy-2-pentenoyl-CoA (forward), and the opposite direction is only achieved by a different, engineered enzyme (5-carboxy-2-pentenoyl-CoA reductase) in adipate biosynthesis.

enzyme_name: Unidentified (non-specific) abscisic-aldehyde reductase of the ABA-alcohol shunt
organism_context: Higher plants; abscisic alcohol accumulates in ABA-aldehyde-oxidase/MoCo-sulfurase mutants (Arabidopsis aba3, tomato flacca/sitiens).
rationale: KEGG R06958 carries no EC and no KO; abscisic alcohol was shown to be a shunt intermediate formed from abscisic aldehyde, but no reductase protein has ever been assigned to this step, so there is no enzyme to classify.
direction_note: The ModelSEED equation is redox-unbalanced — it supplies two protons and no NAD(P)H — so its ΔG′° cannot discriminate direction at all; biologically the aldehyde is reduced to the alcohol in the shunt, which is the written-forward direction the LLM picked.

enzyme_name: Melamine deaminase (s-triazine aminohydrolase), TriA
organism_context: Pseudomonas sp. strain NRRL B-12227 (and Acidovorax); 98% identical to atrazine chlorohydrolase AtzA but with no dehalogenase activity.
rationale: TriA is an amidohydrolase-superfamily deaminase with a single catalytic activity: it removes two of melamine's three amino groups sequentially (melamine -> ammeline -> ammelide), which is one activity applied twice, and its 9-residue divergence from AtzA reflects functional switching, not two activities on one chain.
direction_note: Hydrolytic deamination releasing free ammonia is irreversible under physiological conditions and runs melamine -> ammeline (written-forward); nothing in any organism re-aminates ammeline, so ModelSEED's '<' is biochemically impossible.

enzyme_name: Ammeline aminohydrolase activity of guanine deaminase (GuaD); also the second deamination of melamine deaminase TriA
organism_context: Escherichia coli K-12, Pseudomonas putida KT2440, Bradyrhizobium japonicum USDA 110 and human GDA all deaminate ammeline; TriA does it in dedicated melamine degraders.
rationale: Seffernick et al. identified guanine deaminase as the ammeline-deaminating enzyme and showed the activity is a promiscuous use of the same amidohydrolase active site that deaminates guanine — substrate promiscuity, not a second catalytic activity, so the enzyme stays monofunctional.
direction_note: Hydrolytic deamination with ammonia release is irreversible in the written-forward direction (ammeline -> ammelide); the group-contribution estimate actually agrees ('>'), and only the bronze-grade dGPredictor value supports ModelSEED's '<'.

enzyme_name: N-Cyclopropylmelamine (cyromazine) deaminase — the TriA-type s-triazine aminohydrolase acting on cyromazine
organism_context: s-Triazine-degrading Pseudomonas/Acidovorax (MetaCyc PWY-5171, N-cyclopropylmelamine degradation), the same amidohydrolase lineage as melamine deaminase.
rationale: The catalysing enzyme is the TriA-type amidohydrolase deaminase, a single-activity enzyme whose broad s-triazine specificity lets it strip the first amino group from cyromazine; identity on this specific substrate is inferred from the melamine-deaminase chemistry and MetaCyc pathway assignment rather than a dedicated cyromazine-enzyme paper.
direction_note: Irreversible hydrolytic deamination releasing ammonia, so it runs cyromazine -> N-cyclopropylammeline (written-forward); the group-contribution value also says '>', leaving only bronze-grade dGPredictor behind ModelSEED's '<'.

enzyme_name: N-Cyclopropylammeline deaminase — TriA-type s-triazine aminohydrolase (or a promiscuous guanine-deaminase-type amidohydrolase) acting on N-cyclopropylammeline
organism_context: s-Triazine degraders following MetaCyc PWY-5171; by analogy with the melamine pathway, where the second deamination is done either by TriA itself or by promiscuous guanine deaminase.
rationale: No enzyme has been characterised on this specific substrate; the assignment is by analogy to the ammeline step, where both TriA and guanine deaminase are single-activity amidohydrolases that deaminate the triazine ring as a promiscuous extension of one active site.
direction_note: Hydrolytic deamination is irreversible forward; the group-contribution ΔG′° is strongly negative (−61 kJ/mol, '>'), agreeing with the LLM and against ModelSEED's bronze-grade '<'.

enzyme_name: Ectoine synthase (L-ectoine synthase), EctC
organism_context: Halophilic/halotolerant bacteria — Sphingopyxis alaskensis, Paenibacillus lautus, Halomonas, Chromohalobacter; EctA, EctB and EctC are three separate proteins of the ect operon.
rationale: EctC is a small homodimeric iron-dependent cupin carrying a single activity, the cyclocondensation/water-elimination of N-gamma-acetyl-L-2,4-diaminobutyrate to ectoine; its ability to also use the N-alpha isomer is substrate promiscuity, not a second catalytic activity, and the other ectoine-pathway activities sit on separate EctA/EctB polypeptides.
direction_note: EctC is the committed biosynthetic step and runs N-gamma-ADABA -> ectoine + H2O (written-forward, the LLM's call); ectoine catabolism in vivo proceeds through a separate ectoine hydrolase (DoeA/EutD) rather than by reversing EctC, so ModelSEED's '<' assigns a catabolic hydrolysis to the synthase.

enzyme_name: Rif-Orf5, the putative cytochrome P450 monooxygenase proposed for the oxidative C12/C29 cleavage of rifamycin W
organism_context: Amycolatopsis mediterranei S699; the Δrif-orf5 mutant accumulates rifamycin W congeners, several of them hemiacetals.
rationale: Rif-Orf5 is only a proposed assignment — the enzyme has never been purified or assayed and the mechanism of the oxidative cleavage is explicitly described as uncharacterised — so there is no evidence on which to call it mono- or multifunctional; note also that the 'methane' co-product in the ModelSEED equation is an atom-balancing artifact, not real chemistry.
direction_note: An O2-dependent P450 oxidative ring-cleavage is irreversible in the biosynthetic (written-forward) direction, and the spurious methane term plus the missing O2/reductant make the bronze-grade dGPredictor value behind the '<' call meaningless.

enzyme_name: unknown (unassigned rifamycin tailoring step, rifamycin Z <-> demethyl-desacetyl-rifamycin S)
organism_context: Amycolatopsis mediterranei rifamycin/ansamycin biosynthesis (KEGG rn01051); both compounds are shunt congeners of the pathway.
rationale: KEGG R06995 carries no EC, no KO and no comment, and no publication assigns an enzyme to the interconversion of rifamycin Z and demethyl-desacetyl-rifamycin S, so the catalysing protein cannot be identified at all.
direction_note: ModelSEED writes this as a bare 1:1 interconversion with no cofactor even though the two congeners differ in methylation/acylation state, so the bronze-grade ΔG′° behind the '<' call is computed on an under-specified lumped step rather than a real enzymatic reaction.

enzyme_name: No single enzyme — KEGG-lumped three-step mercapturic-acid sequence: gamma-glutamyltransferase, cysteinylglycine dipeptidase, and cysteine-S-conjugate N-acetyltransferase
organism_context: Mammalian (human/rodent) xenobiotic detoxification; GGT1 at the cell surface, dipeptidase on the brush border, NAT8 in the ER membrane of kidney and liver.
rationale: KEGG flags R07005 as a 'multi-step reaction (see R03916+R04951+R04950)' and 'incomplete reaction': three separate, each monofunctional, enzymes carry it out, so there is no single catalysing protein whose functionality can be classified.
direction_note: The mercapturic-acid pathway is a one-way detoxification route — the GGT-mediated gamma-glutamyl removal and the acetyl-CoA-dependent N-acetylation are both irreversible — so the written-forward direction (GSH conjugate -> mercapturate) is correct, and ModelSEED's '<' would have cells regenerating glutathione conjugates from mercapturates.

enzyme_name: No single enzyme — KEGG-lumped three-step mercapturic-acid sequence: gamma-glutamyltransferase, cysteinylglycine dipeptidase, and cysteine-S-conjugate N-acetyltransferase
organism_context: Mammalian xenobiotic detoxification; (1R)-glutathionyl-(2R)-hydroxy-1,2-dihydronaphthalene regiochemistry from naphthalene oxide conjugation.
rationale: Same situation as rxn04812 — KEGG R07006 is an 'incomplete', explicitly multi-step reaction run by three separate monofunctional enzymes (GGT, a dipeptidase, NAT8), so no single protein catalyses the reaction as written.
direction_note: Irreversible catabolic detoxification sequence: the written-forward direction (GSH conjugate -> N-acetylcysteine conjugate) is the only physiological one, so ModelSEED's '<' inverts a one-way pathway.

enzyme_name: No single enzyme — KEGG-lumped three-step mercapturic-acid sequence: gamma-glutamyltransferase, cysteinylglycine dipeptidase, and cysteine-S-conjugate N-acetyltransferase
organism_context: Mammalian xenobiotic detoxification; (1S,2S) stereoisomer of the naphthalene-derived glutathione conjugate.
rationale: Same as rxn04812/rxn04813 — KEGG R07008 is flagged as a multi-step, incomplete reaction covering three distinct monofunctional enzymes, so there is no single catalysing enzyme to classify; the three stereoisomeric reactions differ only in substrate chirality, not in enzymology.
direction_note: A one-way detoxification sequence with two irreversible steps (gamma-glutamyl transfer and acetyl-CoA-dependent N-acetylation), so the written-forward direction is correct and ModelSEED's '<' is not biochemically realisable.

enzyme_name: None — spontaneous (non-enzymatic) autoxidation of 1,2-dihydroxynaphthalene to 1,2-naphthoquinone
organism_context: Observed both in bacterial naphthalene/naphthalenesulfonate catabolism (Sphingomonas xenophaga BN6, where the autoxidation product acts as a quinoid redox mediator) and in mammalian naphthalene metabolism, where AKR dihydrodiol dehydrogenase makes the catechol which then oxidises in air.
rationale: KEGG R07017 lists no EC and no KO and only the comment 'oxidoreduction'; 1,2-dihydroxynaphthalene is well documented to autoxidise via the semiquinone to 1,2-naphthoquinone, so there is no catalysing enzyme whose functionality could be judged.
direction_note: Autoxidation consumes O2 — omitted from the ModelSEED equation, which balances only the two protons — making the written-forward direction effectively irreversible under aerobic conditions, whereas the reverse (quinone -> catechol) is run in cells by a different enzyme entirely (NAD(P)H quinone oxidoreductase).
